question: Has the Identity MD NFT collection (OpenSea slug identitymd) floor flipped Quotrons Verified (OpenSea collection quotrons404), meaning Identity MD OpenSea listed floor in ETH is strictly greater than Quotrons404 OpenSea listed floor in ETH?

definitions.flip: Answer true only if identitymd_floor > quotrons_floor. Otherwise false. If either floor is unavailable, report inability rather than guessing.
definitions.calendar: Use the latest available OpenSea floors at assessment time within the request window.
definitions.quotrons_floor: Use the current OpenSea listed floor price in ETH for https://opensea.io/collection/quotrons404 (slug quotrons404). Do not use the Sunset collection quotrons.
definitions.identitymd_floor: Use the current OpenSea listed floor price in ETH for https://opensea.io/collection/identitymd (slug identitymd).
OpenSea's listed floorPrice.pricePerItem.token.unit for the Ethereum collection slug identitymd, read as ETH: 1.74.
definitions.quotrons_floor: OpenSea's listed floorPrice.pricePerItem.token.unit for the collection slug quotrons404 (not the Sunset quotrons collection), read as ETH: 1.49999.
definitions.flip: true exactly when the Identity MD listed ETH floor is strictly greater than the Quotrons404 listed ETH floor.
definitions.assessment: The latest OpenSea collection-page values available during the pinned request window were used; unavailable floors would not be inferred.

answer.notes: Read OpenSea's primary collection pages during the pinned assessment window: https://opensea.io/collection/identitymd reported floorPrice.pricePerItem.token.unit 1.74 ETH, and https://opensea.io/collection/quotrons404 reported 1.49999 ETH. Since 1.74 > 1.49999, the requested strict flip is true. This is off-chain panel evidence; the copied Ethereum block window identifies the request window rather than a way to reconstruct marketplace order-book state from RPC logs.
